post: In 2025, BRI ran 315 professional development programs across 27 states and Washington, D. C., reaching over 8,000 teachers. The programs we're most proud of aren't the ones with the highest single-day turnout. They're the ones where we're still showing up years later. Our PD is built around the Founding documents  the Declaration, the Constitution, the Bill of Rights  and the civic principles that come up in every election, every courtroom, and every classroom debate. We design programming to compound: each session builds on the last, and each year gives teachers a deeper foundation to teach from. What would your district's civics program look like with a PD partner for the next 3 years, not just the next 3 weeks? 🔗 Request a program:  https://bit.ly/4fZoZ46  #CivicsEducation  #ProfessionalDevelopment  #AmericanHistory  #K12Education  #ConstitutionDay

Seth Harris's seventh graders dont always get the verdict they hoped for. He makes sure they learn from it. After their mock trial, students examine which arguments persuaded the jury and why. Making their own case is only part of the work. They also have to understand how someone else reached a different conclusion. Congratulations to Seth Harris of Shaker Middle School in Latham, New York, one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Meet the teacher helping students practice thoughtful disagreement:  https://bit.ly/4i74GCm  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Helping students evaluate information and disagree respectfully takes thoughtful teaching. That work deserves recognition. Congratulations to the latest Civic Star Challenge honorees! Together with iCivics, were recognizing teachers who connect the Declaration of Independence to the choices and responsibilities students encounter today. Thank you to Griffin Catalyst, The James Irvine Foundation, Stand Together Trust, and The Pederson Foundation for supporting the teachers behind this work. Meet the honorees:  https://bit.ly/4hG55u7  #CivicEducation  #TeacherAppreciation

"My goal for every student, no matter where they start, is that they leave my classroom believing their voice matters and knowing what to do with it." Katie Boland gives her students at Trumbull High School in Connecticut practice doing just that. They argue Supreme Court cases, consider positions they didnt choose, and learn to listen before preparing a rebuttal. Were proud to recognize Katie as one of the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institutes National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! Read her story:  https://bit.ly/4z7K6HU  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership

Before you click: Which Founder do you think youll get? Put your prediction to the test with BRI's Which Founder Are You? quiz. Discover whose thinking most closely resembles yours, and explore the different perspectives that helped shape self-government. Take the quiz, then tell us in the comments: Who did you get, and did you see it coming?  https://bit.ly/4rkSuBb  #CivicEducation  #AmericanHistory  #FoundingPrinciples

A government strong enough to protect liberty. Limited enough not to threaten it. How could a newly independent nation achieve both? The Articles of Confederation were Americas first answer. Their story is a window into the hard choices of self-government, with real achievements and challenges that put the young republic to the test. Discover why the road to the Constitution was anything but certain. Watch Understanding the Articles of Confederation, part of BRIs Road to the Constitution series:  https://bit.ly/3UVYkNi  #CivicEducation  #AmericanHistory  #Constitution

Seventh graders making their case in a mock trial. High school students preserving veterans' stories. The teachers behind these experiences give students room to think for themselves and help them understand their responsibilities to others. Congratulations to the 10 finalists for the Bill of Rights Institute's National Civics Teacher of the Year Award! From elementary through high school, these educators help students weigh evidence, consider different perspectives, and debate ideas respectfully. We're proud to recognize your work preparing young people for self-government! Meet the finalists:  https://bit.ly/3VkRFfK  #CivicEducation  #TeacherLeadership  #CivicLearning

100,000 secondary teachers. Educators in 91% of U. S. counties. A shared purpose: helping students understand our Founding principles and put citizenship into practice. BRIs Summer 2026 Impact Report shows the work we've done these past few months: - New ways to explore history. The Civics Innovation Lab is testing a Lincoln avatar grounded in scholar-selected sources and an immersive Revolutionary-era print shop. Each pilot starts with teacher and student needs. - Civic learning that starts earlier. BRI Jr. is expanding to help elementary teachers connect history and civics with reading and writing. - Students turning knowledge into service. Medha and Reshma Lalani of Hempfield High School earned the $10,000 MyImpact Challenge National Grand Prize for Tech Buddies, their nonprofit that has helped more than 3,500 older adults build technology skills and confidence. Teachers bring this work into classrooms. Supporters help make it possible. Students carry their learning into their communities. See the people, progress, and possibilities in our Summer 2026 Impact Report:  https://bit.ly/4xvRDyU  #CivicEducation  #StudentLeadership  #EducationPhilanthropy
